true_answer: 'First of all, Leibniz ﬁnds the idea that space and time might be substances or substance-like absurd (see, for example, 'Correspondence with Clarke,' Leibniz's Fourth Paper, §8ﬀ). In short, an empty space would be a substance with no properties; it will be a substance that even God cannot modify or destroy.... That is, space and time are internal or intrinsic features of the complete concepts of things, not extrinsic.... Leibniz's view has two major implications.
